checks: The TGA traveller exemption covers up to a three-month supply of eligible medicines for the traveller or accompanying immediate family. Prescription medicine requires a prescription or clinician letter, and TGA advises original packaging and taking any remainder out on departure.
Specific prohibited or restricted items and applicable alternative approvals require the ODC classification and guidance.

The ODC says the traveller exemption can include personally prescribed controlled medicines within the three-month supply and documentary conditions. The ODC distinguishes goods covered by the exemption from illegal or specially controlled categories.
Australia, controlled medicine in accompanied traveller baggage
Check the ODC prohibited and restricted item guidance by exact active ingredient and formulation.

Austrian Customs distinguishes people living abroad, who may carry medicine needed for themselves or an accompanying pet, from people residing in Austria, whose purchase-abroad allowance is limited to three retail packs per medicine.
Use the health ministry guidance for prescription documentation and special controlled-drug thresholds.

Austria’s health ministry identifies doctor confirmation and translation requirements for prescription medicines. For medicines controlled under the Addictive Substances Act it distinguishes stays up to five days from stays over five and up to 30 days, with a personal requirement ceiling of 30 days.
Austria, medicinal personal-use exception and controlled medicines
Austrian Federal Ministry of Social Affairs and Health
Check medicinal product classification and residency when combining health and customs rules. Where Article 75 applies, use the competent authority documentation framework.

The official royal decree text contains a conditional traveller exemption for legally obtained own-use medicines, with an attestation and a maximum treatment duration, subject to listed substance exclusions.
Belgium, traveller exemption for covered controlled medicines
Belgian Federal Agency for Medicines and Health Products
Read the current consolidated decree and verify excluded schedules and non-Schengen documentation separately. Do not generalize the historical decree to all medicines or routes.
Bulgarian consular guidance points to the Article 75 certificate framework and advises carrying personal quantities of medicines for the trip.
Bulgarian consular guidance, including regulated medicines in Schengen travel
Verify whether national rules for entry from outside Schengen have changed and establish the quantity and permit conditions from a current inbound source.

Current Health Canada guidance permits up to a 90-day supply of eligible prescribed controlled substances, with labelled healthcare packaging and declaration on arrival. Longer needs are referred to the exemptions process. Class A precursor preparations have their own route and quantity conditions.
Canada, prescription controlled medication and Class A precursor travel
Cannabis and CBD are governed separately under CBSA rules. Use the product ingredient and classification to determine applicability.

Croatian Customs describes up to a one-month treatment supply of authorized ordinary medicine with medical evidence, up to five days for medicines containing narcotics, and up to 15 days for qualifying substitution therapy or oncology treatment. It separately describes a certificate exception for residents travelling to Schengen destinations.
Clarify interaction between the general inward limits and incoming Article 75 certificate holders. The published resident exception is written for travel to Schengen countries.

From 1 January 2026 the Danish Medicines Agency permits eligible legally sold personal medicines from any country. The agency lists separate origin and quantity restrictions for antibiotics and evidentiary limits for controlled products.
Denmark, personal medicine in accompanied baggage
Use the current controlled-product page and resolve conflicting doping-medication amount guidance.

The Danish Medicines Agency describes a 30-day supply limit for accompanied medicines in euphoriant schedules B through E, with proof such as a prescription or Schengen certificate. Its guidance prohibits personal imports of schedule A medicines.
Denmark, controlled medicines in traveller baggage
Non-EU/EEA doping-product amount differs between the newer product-specific page and the January change announcement. Seek legal text or written agency clarification.

The State Agency of Medicines distinguishes over-the-counter package limits and permits for justified excess, prescription medicines backed by proof of the prescription, and narcotic or psychotropic medicines subject to route-specific documentary rules.

Use local medicine classification and current route instructions. Article 75 certification by Estonian pharmacies is limited to permanent residents, with separate evidence for medicines bought on travel.

French Customs defines personal-use quantity by treatment duration on the prescription or, for ordinary medicine without one, three months. Accompanied narcotics and psychotropics have a separate therapeutic-quantity rule and require route-specific documents.
France, personal carriage of ordinary, prescription and controlled medicines
Use current Schengen membership and the shared Article 75 certificate rule. The examples in the Customs guidance list an older membership roster.
German Customs describes a personal-needs allowance for medicinal products in passenger baggage and distinguishes same-route baggage carried ahead or afterwards from baggage sent by post.
Germany, ordinary medicines and accompanied traveller baggage
Check statutory conditions for controlled, prohibited and doping products and the right document for non-Schengen arrivals.
Hungarian medicines authority guidance describes different documentation for entering with controlled medicine depending on planned treatment duration.
Hungary, regulated medicines and medical documentation
Verify the current replacement authority’s inbound guidance, national ordinary rules and how treatment periods interact with Article 75.

Iceland’s medicines authority distinguishes ordinary prescription and OTC quantities by EEA departure, controlled medicine by Icelandic residence and where it was acquired, and WADA-listed substances by their own limit. Customs may request proof of medical use.
Iceland, personal medicine carried on entry
Use the regulator table for exact thresholds, proof options and the prescribed basis for quantity.
Italy’s health ministry describes acceptable evidence that personally imported internationally controlled preparations were lawfully supplied in the departure country.
Italy, personally carried internationally controlled medicines
Confirm current ordinary-medicine limits and documentation and validate the national rule for the specific route.

Japan’s health ministry provides category-specific personal medicine quantities exempt from Import Confirmation, including a one-month allowance for most prescriptions and a different general allowance for other drugs. Specified ingredients and unusual forms are exceptions.
Japan, accompanied personal medicines and import confirmation
Japanese Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare
Consult the linked ingredient table and the Narcotics Control Department before using the general exemption for any controlled ingredient.

The Narcotics Control Department distinguishes prior authorization for eligible prescribed narcotics and stimulant raw materials, documentary thresholds for psychotropics, and prohibited substances. Injectable psychotropics are treated differently from non-injectables.
The agency’s classification and quantity tables govern. Special deadlines and permitted arrival ports can vary.

Korea Customs’ November 2026 traveller update describes quantity conditions for eligible personally carried medicines obtained through a healthcare system or pharmacy. The notice expressly excludes medicines with narcotic ingredients and abuse-concern products from that ordinary treatment.
Republic of Korea, passenger clearance notice current November 2026
Use the MFDS approval process for regulated medicines, verify covered products and scope of the new notice before generalizing the quantity treatment.
Latvia’s State Agency of Medicines distinguishes medicines carried in traveller baggage for personal use from postal import and publishes detailed quantity and document guidance.
Latvia, personal medicine carried in baggage
Verify the live agency table and non-Schengen controlled entry conditions. Search indexing exposed the page but full retrieval was blocked.
Mexican consular travel guidance asks passengers carrying medicine for personal use to have a prescription or doctor’s letter documenting the amount for the stay, amount carried and daily dose.
Confirm specific ingredient permissions with domestic customs and health authorities. Broad wording in consular guidance does not resolve regulated-substance exceptions.
Dutch Customs requires accompanied medicines to be for personal use and in original packaging, and may ask for evidence. Medicines covered by the Opium Act require an official statement.
Netherlands, traveller baggage for themselves or their children
For the correct controlled-medicine certificate, verify the traveler’s residence and route. Postal import and veterinary medicines have separate treatment.

Medsafe distinguishes prescription medicines carried in baggage, non-prescription medicines, and controlled medicines. It describes the normal three-month prescription supply, the separate six-month oral contraceptive limit and the one-month controlled supply, with original containers and documentary conditions.
New Zealand, personal medicines carried on entry
New Zealand Medicines and Medical Devices Safety Authority
Follow Ministry of Health declaration and classification guidance for regulated ingredients and separately verify medicinal cannabis authorizations.
The Ministry of Health specifies the controlled-drug traveler exemption, including declaring the medicine on arrival, carrying documentary evidence and a one-month supply limit.
New Zealand, controlled medicines for the traveller or qualifying immediate family member
For medicinal cannabis and other special categories, use the linked national authorities and check the exact product.

Norway’s Medicines Products Agency lists different ordinary medicine quantities for EEA and non-EEA arrivals. It separates doping and narcotic medicine, including evidence and red-channel declaration for covered narcotics and different quantities by residence. Nonresidents exceeding their controlled limit are directed to a permit process.
Norway, medicine brought by a traveller
Use the authority’s exact resident and place-of-supply branches and current permit and medical-cannabis instructions.
Poland’s Chief Pharmaceutical Inspectorate permits personal import of up to five packs of eligible noncontrolled medicinal products and treats controlled ingredients separately.
Official guidance describes documentation for controlled active substances separately.

The Polish inspectorate publishes a current official route to obtain a document authorizing import or export of covered narcotic drugs, psychotropics and category 1 precursors for personal medical purposes.
Poland, controlled medicines for personal travel
Confirm document issuer and mutual recognition for the route. The inspectorate’s advice for applications submitted to it is distinct from the shared Schengen certificate.
Portuguese customs’ passenger guide describes medicine quantities corresponding to personal requirements and carrying the relevant medical prescription.
Portugal, customs passenger guidance on personal medicine
Confirm OTC exceptions, controlled non-Schengen authorization and product classifications.

Singapore HSA distinguishes prohibited medicine from controlled medicine requiring approval and permitted personal prescriptions. The guidance details the supply limit, dispensing labels, approval documentation, an immediate-family exception, and a separate transit-zone provision. Prohibited medicines remain prohibited in transit.
Singapore, traveller medicine and airside transit
Use the agency ingredient checker and schedules for the exact substance. Transit without clearing immigration is distinct from entry with the medicines.

Slovenia’s financial administration describes personal, family and documented third-person medicine carriage from outside the EU, treatment-based allowances and separate certificate controls for narcotics.
Slovenia, travellers arriving from third countries and Schengen controlled medicines
Check the national treatment of non-Schengen controlled arrivals and any other competent-authority conditions.
AEMPS sets out the medical-treatment traveler route for bringing personally used medicines into Spain and a separate procedure for medicines containing narcotic or psychotropic substances.
Spain, national authority framework for accompanied medical-treatment medicines
Spanish Agency of Medicines and Medical Devices
Check the linked FAQs and shared Article 75 certificate for exact exceptions, application conditions and affected ingredient schedules.

Swedish Customs describes passenger medicine for personal medical use with proof, different ordinary quantities for EEA and non-EEA travel, and separately classified narcotic or doping medicines. The authority distinguishes conditional use of the nothing-to-declare lane.
National Medical Products Agency details class- and route-based controlled quantities. A Schengen certificate can be necessary.

Swissmedic distinguishes ordinary medicine’s one-month personal allowance and controlled medicine’s 30 days, with separate certificate templates for arrivals from Schengen and other origins. It states that no longer-quantity authorization exists and refers doping products to the specialized authority.
Switzerland, personal import of ordinary and narcotic medicine
The correct narcotic certificate depends on route. For doping products seek Swiss Sport Integrity instructions.
Thai FDA’s traveler portal provides separate carry-in and carry-out permit workflows, national ingredient schedules and prescribed controlled-medicine instructions.
Thailand, personal travel with narcotic or psychotropic medicines
Check the appropriate schedule and current permit decision and confirm the separate ordinary medicine guidance.

Türkiye’s Ministry of Trade allows certain personal-treatment medicines brought by tourists in reasonable quantities relative to stay, with a physician report, medical organization document or prescription under the applicable resolution.
Türkiye, accompanied passenger medicine for personal treatment
Check the active ingredient and applicable controlled-substance preauthorization or exclusions with the relevant national authority.

EDE distinguishes optional electronic preapproval for qualifying visiting travelers with covered prescribed controlled medicine from the licensed personal-import process. It identifies a treatment-need cap of three months for qualifying narcotic or psychotropic medicine and documentation conditions.
United Arab Emirates, accompanying medicines for qualifying visitors
Check nonvisitor/resident differences, an individual medicine’s listing and permit or declaration route. Avoid treating conditional visitor rules as a universal advance-approval requirement.

UK guidance distinguishes nonresident travelers, who need a prescribing clinician’s letter for covered controlled medicines, from UK residents prescribed controlled medication while overseas, who should contact the Drug and Firearms Licensing Unit.
United Kingdom, personal medicines containing controlled drugs
Consult the linked rules for particular schedules, supply length and exceptions, as well as MHRA for ordinary personal imports.

DEA traveller guidance describes declaring medicines at U.S. customs and label and evidence conditions for personal controlled medication. Its general foreign visitor quantity wording requires reading alongside the governing regulation.
United States, travellers with controlled medicine
Check applicable 21 CFR 1301.26 limits, where the medicine was obtained and prescription/source distinctions. FDA’s separate personal import policy still controls its own approval questions.

Uzbekistan’s personal-use medicines regulation distinguishes base allowances by formulation and pack count, documentation plus declaration for covered excess, and separate schedules, documentation, quantities and mandatory declaration for imported narcotic and psychotropic medicines. The consolidated material describes amendments effective February 2026.
Uzbekistan Cabinet of Ministers, Decree 191, LexUZ publication
Use the controlling Uzbek text for statutory wording, schedules referenced in Decree 330, and formulation-specific thresholds.
